# Instructions

Implement the logic of the hangman game using functional reactive programming.

[Hangman][hangman] is a simple word guessing game.

[Functional Reactive Programming][frp] is a way to write interactive programs.
It differs from the usual perspective in that instead of saying "when the button is pressed increment the counter", you write "the value of the counter is the sum of the number of times the button is pressed."

Implement the basic logic behind hangman using functional reactive programming.
You'll need to install an FRP library for this, this will be described in the language/track specific files of the exercise.

[hangman]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangman_%28game%29
[frp]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_reactive_programming

# Instructions append

## Python Special Instructions

A third party library **is not required** for this exercise.  Please ignore the instructions regarding **FRP library**.


## Exception messages

Sometimes it is necessary to [raise an exception](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html#raising-exceptions). When you do this, you should always include a **meaningful error message** to indicate what the source of the error is. This makes your code more readable and helps significantly with debugging. For situations where you know that the error source will be a certain type, you can choose to raise one of the [built in error types](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#base-classes), but should still include a meaningful message.

This particular exercise requires that you use the [raise statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-raise-statement) to "throw" a `ValueError` when the game has ended but the player tries to continue playing. The tests will only pass if you both `raise` the `exception` and include a message with it.

To raise a `ValueError` with a message, write the message as an argument to the `exception` type:

```python
# when player tries to play, but the game is already over.
raise ValueError("The game has already ended.")
```

Use the instructions above to complete `hangman.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

{"content":"import unittest

from hangman import Hangman, STATUS_LOSE, STATUS_ONGOING, STATUS_WIN


class HangmanTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_initial_state(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        self.assertEqual(game.get_masked_word(), '______')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 9)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_status(), STATUS_ONGOING)
        self.assertEqual(game.status, STATUS_ONGOING)

    def test_correct_guess_reveals_all_occurrences_without_penalty(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        game.guess('a')
        self.assertEqual(game.get_masked_word(), '_a_a_a')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 9)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_status(), STATUS_ONGOING)

    def test_wrong_guess_costs_one_guess(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        game.guess('z')
        self.assertEqual(game.get_masked_word(), '______')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 8)

    def test_repeated_correct_guess_costs_one_guess(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        game.guess('a')
        game.guess('a')
        self.assertEqual(game.get_masked_word(), '_a_a_a')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 8)

    def test_repeated_wrong_guess_costs_one_guess_each_time(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        game.guess('z')
        game.guess('z')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 7)

    def test_tenth_miss_loses(self):
        game = Hangman('a')
        for char in 'bcdefghij':
            game.guess(char)
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 0)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_status(), STATUS_ONGOING)
        game.guess('k')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, -1)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_status(), STATUS_LOSE)
        self.assertEqual(game.status, STATUS_LOSE)

    def test_can_win_with_zero_remaining_guesses(self):
        game = Hangman('banana')
        for char in 'cdefghijk':
            game.guess(char)
        for char in 'ban':
            game.guess(char)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_masked_word(), 'banana')
        self.assertEqual(game.remaining_guesses, 0)
        self.assertEqual(game.get_status(), STATUS_WIN)

    def test_guesses_after_win_or_loss_raise_without_changing_state(self):
        won = Hangman('a')
        won.guess('a')
        lost = Hangman('a')
        for _ in range(10):
            lost.guess('z')
        for game in (won, lost):
            for char in ('a', 'z'):
                with self.subTest(status=game.status, char=char):
                    before = (game.get_masked_word(), game.remaining_guesses,
                              game.get_status())
                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                            ValueError, r'^The game has already ended\.$'):
                        game.guess(char)
                    self.assertEqual(
                        (game.get_masked_word(), game.remaining_guesses,
                         game.get_status()), before)

    def test_games_have_independent_histories(self):
        first = Hangman('banana')
        second = Hangman('banana')
        first.guess('a')
        first.guess('z')
        self.assertEqual(second.get_masked_word(), '______')
        self.assertEqual(second.remaining_guesses, 9)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
